correctness.rationale: Every period-three vertex is static zero or phase-rotating. In a connected 4-regular line graph, contact two gives 2|S| <= number of successor edges <= |E(S)| <= 2|S|, forcing all vertices to rotate and all adjacent phases to differ. This is exactly a proper cubic edge-3-colouring, and conversely every such colouring rotates. The nine-state rung transfer has three diagonal states with cycle-colouring count 2^n+2(-1)^n and six off-diagonal states that swap, contributing six only for even n (straight) or odd n (twisted). Independent direct simulation for n=3,4; proper colouring enumeration n=3..10; and matrix-transfer tests n=3..20 all reproduce the stated formulas. No computation is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A structural bijection for every connected cubic base makes the existence and count of primitive-three excitation equivalent to Tait 3-edge-colourability, a naturally difficult invariant including snark obstructions. For the canonical cubic prism/Möbius families it yields complete exact initial-period-three populations and a surprisingly constant signed seam correction while both totals grow exponentially. This links topology, phase rotations and graph colourings, not an arbitrary small-parameter count.
